regions:regions/fingers/causes/3/signs: A finger catches or locks when bending.
regions:regions/fingers/causes/4/signs: After a knock to the tip, the end of the finger droops and can’t be straightened on its own. It needs a splint soon.
regions:regions/fingers/causes/5/signs: Pain and a weak pinch at the base of the thumb, on the side next to the index finger, after the thumb was bent back (a fall while skiing, or a ball).
regions:regions/fingers/causes/6/signs: Fingers that turn white, then blue, then red in the cold or with stress, with numbness or tingling.
regions:regions/fingers/redFlags/0: A deep cut with loss of movement or feeling in a finger
regions:regions/fingers/redFlags/1: A finger that is swollen, red and very painful to straighten, after a cut or bite (possible tendon sheath infection)
regions:regions/fingers/redFlags/2: A finger or fingertip that stays white, cold or numb
regions:regions/upper-right-abdomen/caus: Severe pain under the right ribs, often after fatty food, maybe spreading to the right shoulder blade. Fever or yellow skin makes it urgent.
A dull ache with tiredness, nausea, yellow eyes or dark urine.
Pain in the back or side that may wrap round to the front, with fever or urinary symptoms.
Pain on movement or pressing one spot, after exertion or coughing.
A burning band of pain followed by a blistering rash on one side.
regions:regions/upper-middle-abdomen/cau: Burning or gnawing pain under the breastbone, bloating, often linked to meals, alcohol or anti-inflammatory painkillers.
Recurring gnawing pain, sometimes at night or when hungry.
Severe pain in the upper middle or right, lasting minutes to hours after food.
Severe pain boring through to the back, with vomiting.
Can feel like indigestion, especially in women, older people and people with diabetes.
regions:regions/upper-middle-abdomen/red: Vomiting blood or “coffee grounds”, or black tarry stools
Severe pain boring through to the back with vomiting
Indigestion-like pain with sweating, breathlessness, or pain spreading to the arm or jaw
regions:regions/upper-left-abdomen/cause: Burning pain and bloating after meals.
Crampy pain under the left ribs that comes and goes, eased by passing wind.
Pain after a blow to the left side, or a dragging ache after glandular fever.
Severe pain going through to the back, with vomiting.
Flank pain wrapping to the front, with fever or urinary symptoms.
Pain on movement or pressing one spot.
regions:regions/right-flank/causes/0/sig: Waves of severe pain from the back or side down toward the groin; can’t get comfortable.
regions:regions/right-flank/causes/1/sig: Side or back pain with fever, shivering and burning when passing urine.
regions:regions/right-flank/causes/2/sig: Pain on bending or twisting, eased by rest.
regions:regions/right-flank/causes/3/sig: Crampy, bloated feeling with infrequent or hard stools.
regions:regions/right-flank/causes/4/sig: A burning band of pain followed by a rash on one side.
regions:regions/around-navel/causes/0/si: Pain often starts here before moving to the lower right, with loss of appetite and nausea.
regions:regions/around-navel/causes/2/si: Bloating and cramps that come and go.
regions:regions/around-navel/causes/3/si: A soft bulge at or near the belly button, more obvious when coughing. A painful, hard bulge that won’t go back is urgent.
regions:regions/around-navel/causes/4/si: Colicky pain, a swollen belly, vomiting, and no wind or stools.
regions:regions/around-navel/causes/5/si: In older adults, especially smokers: a pulsing feeling, or sudden severe pain going to the back.
regions:regions/left-flank/causes/0/sign: Waves of severe pain from the back or side down toward the groin.
regions:regions/left-flank/causes/1/sign: Side or back pain with fever, shivering and burning when passing urine.
regions:regions/left-flank/causes/2/sign: Pain on bending or twisting, eased by rest.
regions:regions/left-flank/causes/3/sign: Crampy pain on the left with bloating and changed bowel habit.
regions:regions/lower-right-abdomen/caus: Pain that starts around the navel and moves here, worse with movement, coughing or bumps in the road, with nausea, loss of appetite and fever.
A bulge in the groin that appears when standing or straining. A painful, hard bulge that won’t go back is urgent.
Severe pain moving from the side down toward the groin.
Recurring pain with diarrhoea and weight loss.

One-sided low pain in someone who could be pregnant, often with vaginal bleeding, pain at the tip of the shoulder, dizziness or fainting. It is an emergency. One on the right can feel like appendicitis.
A cyst can cause a dull one-sided ache. Sudden, severe pain with vomiting can mean the ovary has twisted, which is an emergency.
Cramping that comes and goes and eases after a bowel movement.
regions:regions/lower-middle-abdomen/cau: Low central pain with burning, urgency and passing urine often.
Unable to pass urine, with a tender, full lower belly.
Cramping low central pain around periods.
Low pain with fever, unusual discharge or pain during sex.
Severe period pain, pain during sex or when opening the bowels, and pelvic pain that lasts for months.
Deep pain low in the pelvis or between the scrotum and anus, with burning or difficulty passing urine, sometimes fever.
Cramps and bloating with hard or infrequent stools.
Any significant lower abdominal pain in pregnancy, or with a missed period, should be assessed promptly.
regions:regions/lower-left-abdomen/cause: Pain here with fever and tenderness, mostly in older adults.
Cramping and bloating linked to bowel habit.
A groin bulge when standing or straining.
Severe pain moving from the side down toward the groin.
One-sided low pain in someone who could be pregnant, often with vaginal bleeding, pain at the tip of the shoulder, dizziness or fainting. It is an emergency.
A cyst can cause a dull one-sided ache. Sudden, severe pain with vomiting can mean the ovary has twisted, which is an emergency.
Recurring pain with bloody diarrhoea or urgency.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/0/signs: Burning or stinging when passing urine, needing to go often, cloudy or smelly urine. Fever, shivering or pain in the side means the kidneys may be involved.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/1/signs: Unusual discharge, burning when passing urine, sores, blisters or lumps. Many have no symptoms. Sexual health clinics test and treat confidentially.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/2/signs: Itching and soreness of the vulva with a thick white discharge. A pharmacy treatment works for most; see a doctor if it keeps coming back.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/3/signs: A swelling on one side of the vaginal opening. A painful, hot, growing one may be an abscess.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/4/signs: Burning, stinging or soreness of the vulva lasting months, sometimes only on touch or during sex.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/5/signs: Sudden, severe pain in one testicle, often with swelling, belly pain and vomiting, most often in teenagers. It is an emergency: surgery within hours saves the testicle.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/6/signs: Pain and swelling at the back of a testicle building up over a day or two, sometimes with fever or burning when passing urine.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/7/signs: A painless lump, a swelling or a heavy feeling in the scrotum. Most lumps are harmless, but all need checking.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/8/signs: A bulge that comes down into the scrotum when standing or straining. A tender, hard swelling that won’t go back is urgent.
regions:regions/genitals/causes/9/signs: Burning or stabbing pain in the genitals or perineum, worse sitting and eased by standing or lying down.
regions:regions/genitals/redFlags/0: Sudden, severe pain in a testicle
regions:regions/genitals/redFlags/1: An erection lasting more than four hours
regions:regions/genitals/redFlags/2: Heavy bleeding, or severe pain, in pregnancy
regions:regions/genitals/redFlags/4: Numbness around the genitals or buttocks with new bladder or bowel problems (possible cauda equina syndrome)
regions:regions/hip-groin/causes/0/signs: Groin or thigh pain and stiffness, worse with walking, trouble with shoes and socks.
regions:regions/hip-groin/causes/1/signs: Pain on the inner thigh after kicking, sprinting or changing direction.
regions:regions/hip-groin/causes/2/signs: An older person who can’t bear weight after a fall.
regions:regions/hip-groin/causes/3/signs: Pain on the outer hip, worse lying on that side or climbing stairs.
regions:regions/hip-groin/causes/4/signs: A groin bulge when standing or straining.
regions:regions/hip-groin/causes/5/signs: A problem in the testicle, such as torsion or epididymitis, is often felt in the groin. Sudden, severe pain is an emergency.
regions:regions/hip-groin/causes/6/signs: Hip or buttock pain with back stiffness, sometimes running down the leg.
regions:regions/hip-groin/redFlags/0: A child with a limp and fever, or who refuses to walk
regions:regions/hip-groin/redFlags/1: An older person who can’t bear weight after a fall
regions:regions/hip-groin/redFlags/2: Sudden, severe pain in a testicle, or groin pain with a swollen scrotum
regions:regions/thigh/causes/0/signs: A sudden pull at the front or inner thigh while sprinting, kicking or changing direction.
regions:regions/thigh/causes/1/signs: A painful, stiff thigh after a knee or a blow to the front of the thigh, with bruising. It settles over days to weeks.
regions:regions/thigh/causes/2/signs: Burning or numbness on the outer thigh from a squeezed skin nerve.
regions:regions/thigh/causes/3/signs: A swollen, warm, painful leg, often after travel, surgery or immobility.
regions:regions/thigh/causes/4/signs: Severe pain and deformity after major trauma.
regions:regions/thigh/causes/5/signs: Thigh pain can come from the hip or the lower back.
regions:regions/thigh/redFlags/0: A swollen, painful leg with breathlessness or chest pain: call emergency services
regions:regions/thigh/redFlags/1: Severe pain and swelling after a blow that keeps getting worse
regions:regions/back-of-thigh/causes/0/s: A sudden sharp pain or pull at the back of the thigh while sprinting or kicking, sometimes with bruising a day or two later.
regions:regions/back-of-thigh/causes/1/s: A pop with sudden weakness and a lot of bruising down the back of the thigh. A tear near the sitting bone may need repair.
regions:regions/back-of-thigh/causes/2/s: Pain running from the buttock down the back of the thigh, often past the knee, with tingling or numbness. It usually comes from the lower back.
regions:regions/back-of-thigh/causes/3/s: A brief, hard tightening of the muscle, often at night or during exercise.
regions:regions/back-of-thigh/causes/4/s: A swollen, warm, painful leg, often after travel, surgery or being unwell in bed.
regions:regions/back-of-thigh/redFlags/0: A swollen, painful leg with breathlessness or chest pain: call emergency services
regions:regions/back-of-thigh/redFlags/1: Numbness around the genitals or buttocks, new bladder or bowel problems, or weakness in both legs: emergency (possible cauda equina syndrome)
regions:regions/back-of-thigh/redFlags/2: A leg that is getting weaker
regions:regions/knee/causes/0/signs: Ache around the kneecap on stairs, squatting or after sitting.
regions:regions/knee/causes/1/signs: Pain just below the kneecap when jumping, squatting or climbing stairs, common in jumping sports.
regions:regions/knee/causes/2/signs: A twist or pop with swelling and a knee that gives way.
regions:regions/knee/causes/3/signs: Joint-line pain, catching or locking after a twist.
regions:regions/knee/causes/4/signs: Pain and stiffness in older adults, worse with activity.
regions:regions/knee/causes/5/signs: Sharp pain on the outer knee in runners and cyclists, worse going downhill.
regions:regions/knee/causes/6/signs: A swelling over or below the kneecap after kneeling a lot.
regions:regions/knee/causes/7/signs: A swelling or tight feeling behind the knee, often alongside arthritis. A suddenly swollen, painful calf needs checking for a clot (DVT).
regions:regions/knee/causes/8/signs: A red, hot, swollen knee, with or without fever, can be gout or infection.
regions:regions/knee/redFlags/0: A hot, swollen joint with fever
regions:regions/knee/redFlags/1: Unable to bear weight or straighten the knee after an injury
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/0/si: A soft swelling behind the knee, tight when you bend it, often with arthritis or a meniscus tear. If it bursts, the calf becomes swollen and painful like a blood clot, so get that checked the same day.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/1/si: Pain at the inner or outer back of the knee after sprinting or kicking, worse bending the knee against resistance.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/2/si: A sudden pull at the top of the calf during a push-off, then pain on walking or rising on tiptoe.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/3/si: Pain at the back and outer side of the knee, worse walking or running downhill.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/4/si: Pain deep in the back of the knee on squatting or twisting, sometimes with catching or locking.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/5/si: Pain at the back of the knee after a blow to the front of the shin with the knee bent, or a fall onto the bent knee.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/6/si: A swollen, warm, painful calf or back of the knee, especially after travel, surgery or illness.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/7/si: Pain behind the knee as part of a line of pain from the buttock down the back of the leg, often with tingling or numbness.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/causes/8/si: A pulsing lump behind the knee in an older adult, or calf cramping on exercise in a young athlete that settles at rest.
regions:regions/back-of-knee/redFlags/0: A swollen, warm, painful calf: same-day assessment (possible DVT)
regions:regions/back-of-knee/redFlags/1: Sudden breathlessness or chest pain with a swollen leg: call emergency services
regions:regions/back-of-knee/redFlags/2: A cold, pale, numb or painful foot
regions:regions/back-of-knee/redFlags/3: A badly injured knee that looks out of shape: emergency care (a dislocated knee can tear the artery behind it)
regions:regions/lower-leg/causes/0/signs: Diffuse pain along the inner shin with running.
regions:regions/lower-leg/causes/1/signs: One very tender spot on the shin that is getting worse.
regions:regions/lower-leg/causes/2/signs: A tight, aching front of the shin that builds up during running and eases with rest, sometimes with tingling on top of the foot.
regions:regions/lower-leg/causes/3/signs: A painful lump after knocking the shin. The thin skin over the bone can be slow to heal.
regions:regions/lower-leg/causes/4/signs: A red, hot, swollen, tender patch of skin that spreads, sometimes with a fever.
regions:regions/lower-leg/redFlags/0: Severe, increasing pain after an injury or in a tight cast
regions:regions/lower-leg/redFlags/1: Red, hot, swollen skin that is spreading fast, with a fever or feeling very unwell
regions:regions/calf/causes/0/signs: A sudden pull or a feeling of being struck in the calf when pushing off, followed by tightness.
regions:regions/calf/causes/1/signs: Brief, intense tightening, often at night.
regions:regions/calf/causes/2/signs: Pain and stiffness in the tendon just above the heel, worst in the morning or at the start of exercise.
regions:regions/calf/causes/3/signs: Bulging, twisted veins with aching or heavy legs, worse at the end of the day.
regions:regions/calf/causes/4/signs: Pain or tingling down the back of the leg into the calf or foot, coming from a nerve root in the lower back.
regions:regions/calf/causes/5/signs: Cramping calf pain on walking that eases with rest.
regions:regions/calf/causes/6/signs: A swollen, warm, tender calf, especially after travel, surgery or immobility.
regions:regions/calf/causes/7/signs: A sudden snap, or a feeling of being kicked in the back of the ankle, then trouble walking or standing on tiptoe.
regions:regions/calf/redFlags/0: A swollen, painful calf with breathlessness or chest pain: call emergency services (possible blood clot in the lung)
regions:regions/calf/redFlags/1: Severe, increasing pain after an injury or in a tight cast
regions:regions/calf/redFlags/2: A cold, pale or blue foot or leg
regions:regions/ankle/causes/0/signs: Swelling and bruising after rolling the ankle. If you can’t take four steps or the bone is tender, get it checked.
regions:regions/ankle/causes/1/signs: Pain and swelling behind the outer ankle bone, often after a sprain or with a high arch.
regions:regions/ankle/causes/2/signs: Pain and swelling behind the inner ankle bone, with the arch slowly dropping. A common cause of adult flat foot.
regions:regions/ankle/causes/3/signs: Stiffness, swelling and aching in the ankle, often years after a bad sprain or a break.
regions:regions/ankle/causes/4/signs: Unable to bear weight, a deformed ankle, or tenderness right on the bone after a twist or a fall.
regions:regions/ankle/redFlags/0: An ankle that looks out of shape after an injury, or an open wound over the bone
regions:regions/ankle/redFlags/1: Unable to take four steps after an injury
regions:regions/ankle/redFlags/2: A cold, pale or blue foot
regions:regions/ankle/redFlags/3: A hot, swollen joint with fever
regions:regions/top-of-foot/causes/0/sig: Aching or tingling on the top of the foot from tight laces or new shoes, easing when they come off.
regions:regions/top-of-foot/causes/1/tit: Tendon pain on top of the foot
regions:regions/top-of-foot/causes/1/sig: Aching along the top of the foot that is worse when you run or pull the toes up.
regions:regions/top-of-foot/causes/2/sig: Aching and a bony bump on top of the middle of the foot, worse in tight shoes.
regions:regions/top-of-foot/causes/3/sig: Pain on top of the foot that builds with walking or running, with one tender spot on a bone, after doing more than usual.
regions:regions/top-of-foot/causes/4/sig: Any wound, blister, colour change or swelling on the foot of someone with diabetes needs a prompt check, even if it doesn’t hurt.
regions:regions/top-of-foot/causes/5/sig: Pain and swelling across the middle of the foot, with bruising on the sole, after a twist or a fall. It is easy to miss and needs an X-ray.
regions:regions/top-of-foot/redFlags/0: Bruising on the sole after an injury, or being unable to bear weight
regions:regions/top-of-foot/redFlags/1: A new wound, blister, colour change or swelling on the foot if you have diabetes
regions:regions/top-of-foot/redFlags/2: A cold, pale or blue foot
regions:regions/toes/causes/0/signs: A painful, red edge of the toenail, usually the big toe, digging into the skin, sometimes infected.
regions:regions/toes/causes/1/signs: Pain, swelling and bruising after stubbing or dropping something on a toe. A big toe that is broken or a toe that looks crooked needs checking.
regions:regions/toes/causes/2/signs: A bony bump at the side of the big-toe joint, with the big toe leaning towards the others.
regions:regions/toes/causes/3/signs: Toes bent at the middle joint, rubbing on shoes and forming corns.
regions:regions/toes/causes/4/title: Pain under the ball of the foot
regions:regions/toes/causes/4/signs: Aching or burning under the ball of the foot, worse in thin-soled or high-heeled shoes.
regions:regions/toes/causes/5/signs: Burning pain, numbness or a feeling of a pebble in the shoe between the third and fourth toes.
regions:regions/toes/causes/6/signs: A sudden, very painful, red, hot and swollen big-toe joint, often starting at night. Even a bed sheet touching it hurts.
regions:regions/toes/redFlags/0: A toe that turns black, blue or very pale
regions:regions/toes/redFlags/1: A red, hot, swollen joint with fever
regions:regions/toes/redFlags/2: A new wound or blister on the foot if you have diabetes
regions:regions/heel/causes/0/signs: Sharp pain under the heel with the first steps in the morning or after sitting, easing as you walk.
regions:regions/heel/causes/1/signs: Pain and stiffness in the cord above the heel, worst in the morning or at the start of exercise.
regions:regions/heel/causes/2/signs: A sudden snap, as if kicked in the heel, then you can't push off or stand on tiptoe.
regions:regions/heel/causes/3/signs: Heel pain in an active child of about 8 to 14, worse with running and jumping, where the Achilles pulls on the growing heel bone. It settles with growth.
regions:regions/heel/causes/4/signs: Heel pain that builds with walking or running and the whole heel is tender when squeezed, after a rise in activity.
regions:regions/heel/causes/5/signs: Burning, tingling or numbness under the heel and sole, sometimes worse at night.
regions:regions/heel/causes/6/signs: A tender, sometimes red bump at the back of the heel where the shoe rubs, just below the Achilles tendon.
regions:regions/heel/causes/7/signs: A deep ache in the middle of the heel pad, worse walking barefoot on hard floors, often after a jump or a landing.
regions:regions/heel/causes/8/signs: Pain in both heels, or at the Achilles and under the heel together, with morning back stiffness, psoriasis or swollen joints elsewhere.
regions:regions/heel/redFlags/0: A sudden snap at the back of the heel and you can't push off or stand on tiptoe
regions:regions/heel/redFlags/1: A hot, red, swollen heel or foot with fever, or a new wound on the foot if you have diabetes
regions:regions/heel/redFlags/2: Heel pain after a fall from a height that stops you bearing weight
regions:regions/heel/redFlags/3: A cold, pale or numb foot, or a heel sore that isn't healing
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/0/sign: Aching between the shoulder blades after long sitting.
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/1/sign: Sharp pain beside the spine when breathing or twisting.
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/2/sign: Sudden mid-back pain after minor strain in someone with thin bones.
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/3/sign: A burning band of pain followed by a rash on one side.
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/4/sign: The heart, aorta, gallbladder or pancreas can cause upper-back pain.
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/5/sign: Pain between or over a shoulder blade, often with neck pain and pins and needles, numbness or weakness down one arm.
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/6/sign: Sharp pain on breathing in or coughing, with a cough, fever or breathlessness.
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/7/titl: Rounded upper back in a teenager (Scheuermann’s disease)
regions:regions/upper-back/causes/7/sign: An aching, stiff upper back and a curve that doesn't straighten when standing tall, usually noticed in the early teens.
regions:regions/upper-back/redFlags/0: Sudden, severe tearing pain between the shoulder blades
regions:regions/upper-back/redFlags/1: Back pain with chest pain or breathlessness
regions:regions/upper-back/redFlags/2: Back pain with fever, unexplained weight loss or a history of cancer
regions:regions/upper-back/redFlags/3: New numbness or weakness in the arms or legs, or bladder or bowel problems
regions:regions/mid-back/causes/0/signs: Aching or sharp pain beside the spine after lifting, twisting or long sitting, worse with some movements. Staying active helps.
regions:regions/mid-back/causes/1/signs: Sharp, one-sided pain beside the spine that catches on breathing in, twisting or coughing.
regions:regions/mid-back/causes/2/signs: Sudden mid-back pain after a minor strain, cough or fall in someone over 60 or with thin bones, sometimes with loss of height.
regions:regions/mid-back/causes/3/signs: Burning or tingling pain in a band around one side of the chest and back, followed a few days later by a blistering rash. See a doctor early for antiviral treatment.
regions:regions/mid-back/causes/4/signs: Pain at the bottom of the ribs on one side of the back, with fever, shivering or urinary symptoms, or waves of severe pain spreading to the groin.
regions:regions/mid-back/causes/5/signs: Gallstones, a stomach ulcer or pancreatitis can be felt in the middle of the back, often after eating and with pain in the upper abdomen.
regions:regions/mid-back/causes/6/signs: Sharp pain in the side of the back on breathing in or coughing, with a cough, fever or breathlessness.
regions:regions/mid-back/causes/7/signs: Stiffness that is worst in the morning, lasts over 30 minutes and eases with exercise, starting before 40. Sometimes with pain where the ribs meet the spine.
regions:regions/mid-back/redFlags/0: Sudden, severe tearing pain in the back: call emergency services (possible aortic dissection)
regions:regions/mid-back/redFlags/1: Back pain with chest pain, breathlessness or sweating: call emergency services
regions:regions/mid-back/redFlags/2: Back pain with fever, unexplained weight loss or a history of cancer
regions:regions/mid-back/redFlags/3: New numbness or weakness in the legs, or bladder or bowel problems
regions:regions/mid-back/redFlags/4: Back pain after a serious fall or accident
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/0/sign: Pain and stiffness after lifting, bending or nothing in particular. Usually settles within weeks, and staying active helps.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/1/sign: Pain shooting down the back of the leg, often with tingling.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/2/sign: One-sided low-back and buttock pain, worse on stairs or rolling in bed.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/3/sign: Pain higher up in the side or back, with fever or urinary symptoms.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/4/sign: Leg pain or heaviness on walking, relieved by sitting or bending forward.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/5/sign: Stiffness worst in the morning, lasting over 30 minutes and easing with exercise, starting before 40.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/6/sign: Sudden pain in the lower back after a minor strain, cough or fall in someone over 60 or with thin bones, sometimes with loss of height.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/7/sign: A dull ache in the lower back and lower abdomen around periods. Pain that is severe, getting worse, or there between periods needs a doctor.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/8/sign: Aching in the lower back, between the legs or in the tip of the penis, with painful or frequent passing of urine, sometimes with fever.
regions:regions/lower-back/causes/9/sign: A widened aorta usually causes no symptoms, but if it leaks it causes sudden, severe pain in the lower back or belly, often with feeling faint. Most likely in men over 65 and smokers. This is an emergency.
regions:regions/lower-back/redFlags/0: Numbness around the genitals or buttocks, new bladder or bowel problems, or weakness in both legs: emergency (possible cauda equina syndrome)
regions:regions/lower-back/redFlags/1: Back pain with fever, unexplained weight loss, a history of cancer, or after significant trauma
regions:regions/lower-back/redFlags/2: Severe pain that is worse at night and doesn’t ease with rest
regions:regions/lower-back/redFlags/3: Sudden, severe lower back or belly pain in an older adult, especially with fainting: call emergency services (possible leaking aortic aneurysm)
regions:regions/tailbone/causes/0/signs: Pain at the very bottom of the spine, worse sitting or getting up from a chair, often after a fall or childbirth.
regions:regions/tailbone/causes/1/signs: Pain after a fall onto your bottom, worse when sitting or getting up. It usually settles over a few weeks, and a cushion with a gap at the back helps.
regions:regions/tailbone/causes/2/signs: A painful, swollen, sometimes discharging lump in the skin at the top of the buttock crease.
regions:regions/tailbone/causes/3/title: Piles or a tear at the back passage
regions:regions/tailbone/causes/3/signs: Pain or itching around the back passage when opening your bowels, sometimes with bright red blood on the paper. Bleeding that keeps happening, or at over 50, should be checked by a doctor.
regions:regions/tailbone/causes/4/signs: The lower spine and the sacroiliac joints can cause an ache that is felt down at the tailbone.
regions:regions/tailbone/redFlags/0: Numbness around the genitals or buttocks, new bladder or bowel problems, or weakness in both legs: emergency (possible cauda equina syndrome)
regions:regions/tailbone/redFlags/1: A hot, swollen, very painful lump near the tailbone or back passage with fever
regions:regions/tailbone/redFlags/2: Tailbone pain with fever, unexplained weight loss or a history of cancer
regions:regions/buttock/causes/0/signs: Pain from the buttock shooting down the back of the leg, often with tingling or numbness. It usually comes from an irritated nerve root in the lower back.
regions:regions/buttock/causes/1/signs: A deep ache in the middle of the buttock, worse sitting or on stairs, sometimes with tingling down the back of the thigh.
regions:regions/buttock/causes/2/signs: One-sided pain over the dimple at the top of the buttock, worse on stairs, standing up or rolling in bed.
regions:regions/buttock/causes/3/signs: Aching or tightness in the buttock after running, climbing or a sudden effort, easing over days to weeks.
regions:regions/buttock/causes/4/signs: Deep pain at the bottom of the buttock, worse sitting on hard chairs or running uphill.
regions:regions/buttock/causes/5/signs: Hip arthritis can ache in the buttock as well as the groin, with stiffness putting on shoes and socks.
regions:regions/buttock/causes/6/signs: A deep ache low in the buttock, worse with long strides or when the thigh is turned in, from the quadratus femoris being pinched between the sitting bone and the femur.
regions:regions/buttock/causes/7/title: Hamstring tear at the sitting bone
regions:regions/buttock/causes/7/signs: A sudden sharp pain or pop at the bottom of the buttock while sprinting, water-skiing or doing the splits, followed by bruising down the back of the thigh. A complete tear may need surgery within weeks, so see a doctor promptly.
regions:regions/buttock/redFlags/0: Numbness around the genitals or buttocks, new bladder or bowel problems, or weakness in both legs: emergency (possible cauda equina syndrome)
regions:regions/buttock/redFlags/1: A leg that is getting weaker, or buttock pain with fever or feeling very unwell
regions:regions/buttock/redFlags/2: Unable to bear weight after a fall
regions:regions/buttock/redFlags/3: Severe pain in the hip or buttock after a fall, with a leg that looks shorter or turned outwards: possible broken hip
